newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: GiroCredit mulls Macedonian bank stake.
newsitem.headline: GiroCredit mulls Macedonian bank stake.

text.p: Austria's GiroCredit Bank AG may acquire around 35 percent in Macedonia's biggest state-owned bank Stopanska Banka, bank officials said.

"We are in negotiations with an Austrian Bank for selling stake in Stopanska Banka...We expect to sell to this investor a stake of around 35 percent," Vice Governor of the National Bank of Macedonia (NBM) Gligor Bishev told Reuters.
A Stopanska Banka official, who declined to be named, said the bank was in talks with GiroCredit and the deal was expected to be finalised soon.
Stopanska Banka was one of several local banks placed on a rehabilitation programme, backed by the World Bank, which was recently completed. Its share capital is around $50 million.
Bishev said that the European Bank for Development and Reconstruction and International Finance Corporation were also in talks with Stopanska Banka.
"If the deal is finalised the three investors will hold more than 50 percent in Stopanska Banka," said Bishev.
Macedonia has 21 universal banks, of which nine have some form of foreign participation, mostly from the EBRD, Slovenia and Croatia.
Foreign banks are scarce so far. Russia's Akabank is the only foreign bank with a branch in Skopje. Balkanska Banka AD was set up in Skopje by two Bulgarian banks and Macedonian firms four years ago.

"The most difficult stage of bank reforms is behind us. The share of non-performing loans in total loan portfolios was reduced from 85 percent at the end of 93 to 32 percent at the end of September 1996," said Bishev.

He did not see serious stabilisation problems in the banking sector as the national currency, the denar, has been remarkably steady trading around 40 per dollar over the past three years. The NBM fixed rate for Friday was 44.5 denars per dollar.

Macedonia's banks have yet to build their capacity to access risk and make good loans to the economy, said the World Bank. Attracting foreign investors was one of the ways to improve corporate governance.

Under central bank licencing requirements, banks need nine million German marks for a full license and three million marks for domestic operations. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
